databaselibraryreadingslab

“The spectacle is not a collection of images; it is a social relation between people that is mediated by images.”

Guy Debord, The Society of the Spectacle, thesis 4 1

1 a relation between people, and not a quantity of images

  • “In societies where modern conditions of production prevail, life is presented as an immense accumulation of spectacles. Everything that was directly lived has receded into a representation.” thesis 1 · p. 1
  • “The spectacle cannot be understood as a mere visual excess produced by mass-media technologies. It is a worldview that has actually been materialized, that has become an objective reality.” thesis 5 · p. 1

2 what the relation is made of

  • “Understood in its totality, the spectacle is both the result and the project of the present mode of production. It is not a mere supplement or decoration added to the real world, it is the heart of this real society's unreality.” thesis 6 · p. 2
  • “The spectacle is capital accumulated to the point that it becomes images.” thesis 34 · p. 10
  • “The spectacle is the stage at which the commodity has succeeded in totally colonizing social life. Commodification is not only visible, we no longer see anything else; the world we see is the world of the commodity.” thesis 42 · p. 15

3 what it does to the people inside it

  • “In the spectacle, a part of the world represents itself to the world and is superior to it. The spectacle is simply the common language of this separation.” thesis 29 · p. 9
  • “the more he identifies with the dominant images of need, the less he understands his own life and his own desires” thesis 30 · p. 10
  • “The spectacle's social function is the concrete manufacture of alienation.” thesis 32 · p. 10
  • “While eliminating geographical distance, this society produces a new internal distance in the form of spectacular separation.” thesis 167 · p. 89

4 the two forms it takes, and the one who speaks for it

  • “The spectacle exists in a concentrated form or a diffuse form, depending on the requirements of the particular stage of poverty it denies and supports. In both cases it is nothing more than an image of happy harmony surrounded by desolation and horror, at the calm center of misery.” thesis 63 · p. 25
  • “The agent of the spectacle who is put on stage as a star is the opposite of an individual; he is as clearly the enemy of his own individuality as of the individuality of others.” thesis 61 · p. 23

5 its time

  • “Examining history amounts to examining the nature of power.” thesis 134 · p. 71
  • “The irreversible time of production is first of all the measure of commodities.” thesis 146 · p. 79
  • “The spectacle, considered as the reigning society's method for paralyzing history and memory and for suppressing any history based on historical time, represents a false consciousness of time.” thesis 158 · p. 84

6 its culture, and the way out of it

  • “As culture becomes completely commodified it tends to become the star commodity of spectacular society.” thesis 193 · p. 103
  • “Dadaism sought to abolish art without realizing it; Surrealism sought to realize art without abolishing it.” thesis 191 · p. 102
  • “The real values of culture can be maintained only by actually negating culture.” thesis 210 · p. 110
  • “Detournement is the flexible language of anti-ideology.” thesis 208 · p. 109
  • “The self-emancipation of our time is an emancipation from the material bases of inverted truth.” thesis 221 · p. 116

source: writings/The Society of the Spectacle - Guy Debord.pdf — Guy Debord, The Society of the Spectacle, translated by Ken Knabb, 221 numbered theses. Thesis numbers and page numbers are the book's own.
